extends: REQ-ARC-WMTE-5725 (the n<=6, 8192-budget, single-GPU prior). Three operator-requested changes: 16384 budget (2x), larger N (up to the 20-game usable ceiling), dual-GPU ThinkingCap serving topology. BOTH generators re-measured FRESH at 16384 (5725's 8192 Qwen baseline NOT reused -- the budget change makes it an unfair comparator).
question: At a DOUBLED 16384-token budget and larger N, does ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B (genuine /think via its chat template) COMPLETE the seeded induction more often than vanilla Qwen3.5-9B-MTP, and is any edge statistically distinguishable? Secondary: does the dual-GPU FFN+MTP-draft split speed the 27B up or does cross-GPU PCIe overhead eat the gain?

model_specs.name: ThinkingCap-Qwen3.6-27B
model_specs.role: TREATMENT generator (TREATMENT: RL-tuned for ~50%-fewer-thinking-tokens (Qwen3.6-27B hybrid SSM+attn, Q4_K_M)); /v1/chat/completions (use_chat_template=True, the 5725 fix)

dual_gpu_topology.description: 16GB Q4 on 2x RTX 3090: FFN tensors (blk.N.ffn_{down,gate,up}, the largest tensor class) -> CUDA0 via -ot ffn=CUDA0; main attention + SSM + KV cache -> CUDA1 via -ts 0,1; the nextn MTP self-draft -> CUDA0 via -otd nextn=CUDA0 when MTP on. Approximates a Kaggle L4x4 multi-GPU allocation; NOT the submission-kernel config.

model_specs.server: CUDA llama-server, -ngl 999, q8_0 KV, n_ctx=32768, -fit off (Qwen3.6-27B hybrid SSM+attn), port 8969

model_specs.name: Qwen3.5-9B-MTP
model_specs.role: BASELINE generator (the FROZEN live generator (re-measured fresh at 16384 as the matched reason baseline)); raw /completion path (Qwen tolerates /think); re-measured FRESH at 16384
model_specs.server: CUDA llama-server single-GPU (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1), -ngl 999, q8_0 KV, MTP on, port 8968

field_principles.honest_verdict: terminal-prefixed self-declared state; numbers-first, no interpretive 'cleared the wall' gloss -- a completion delta at N game pairs is reported with its Wilcoxon p, never overclaimed.
field_principles.inference_substrate: live_llm_inference -- both generators really induce on live CUDA llama-servers at a 16384 budget; per-cell durations disclosed.
field_principles.random_seed: LLM sampling is stochastic; trials are per-game replicates (NOT independent game-level samples) -- we pair by GAME and report Wilcoxon + sign test + fragility.
field_principles.reproducibility_checksum: content hash over harness+driver code + generator/topology config + rows.
field_principles.solve_provenance: development_proxy -- PUBLIC-game offline dev measurement of the LIVE induce->plan->execute mechanism with the generator swapped, NOT a hidden-game solve.
field_principles.verifier_is_oracle: False -- the win oracle is the level counter; hand_verifier is only a dense progress MEASUREMENT, oracle-distinct.
field_principles.preconditions_checked: GGUF cache + REAL GPU offload (VRAM jump) + a coherence+tok/s smoke test of the dual-GPU topology verified BEFORE the full run (a cross-GPU split that loads can still silently corrupt output).
field_principles.induce_ok: PRIMARY: did the cell finish reasoning + emit parseable engine+is_level_complete code BEFORE the 16384-token limit -- the token-efficiency test at the doubled budget.
field_principles.dual_gpu_topology: records the exact FFN/MTP-draft/attention placement so the speed-vs-single-GPU comparison is reproducible; whether it helped is REPORTED, not assumed.

sample_size.paired_unit: game (metrics averaged over trials, paired by game)
sample_size.primary_test: Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-game induce_ok deltas (more powered than the binary sign test at this N); sign test + fragility reported alongside.
sample_size.sample_size_ceiling_note: N>=30 UNIQUE games is MATHEMATICALLY UNREACHABLE: only 25 public games exist in ops/arc_solve_registry.yaml, of which 20 supply a valid seeded level-up window (5 fail: wa30/sc25/tn36 have no hand_verifier adapter, ka59 hits a coordinate-parse ValueError in build_window, dc22 returns None). This run uses N=20 game pairs. If N < 20, the roster was further bounded to keep the autonomous conductor's downtime reasonable (this run needs GPU 0); that is a downtime bound, NOT a fresh statistical ceiling -- the true usable ceiling is 20 games. Trials-per-game (2) add stability on each game's own estimate but are NOT additional independent degrees of freedom for the paired-by-game test (same game, same seeded window).

dual_gpu_topology_smoke.note: coherence + tok/s of each candidate ThinkingCap topology, measured on 2 real induction-shaped prompts BEFORE the full run. The full run used the fastest COHERENT config. A cross-GPU tensor split that loads without error can still silently corrupt output, so coherence is a hard gate.

configs.coherence_basis: both smoke prompts (ls20, ft09) produced real, readable <think> reasoning about the actual induction task (ls20: 'The user wants me to induce a world model...'; ft09: 'Let me analyze this ARC task carefully...'); worst_40char_rep=1 (no degeneration). NOTE: the smoke's automated `coherent` boolean was mis-calibrated (frac_unique>0.02 threshold is too strict for long natural-language text, which naturally has ~0.015-0.02 unique-char ratio) and false-flagged these as incoherent; coherence was confirmed by reading the HEAD/TAIL + the near-zero repetition count.

manual validation with a fixed add(a,b) reasoning+code prompt: emitted real 'Thinking Process: 1. Analyze the Request...' reasoning followed by CORRECT code (```python def add(a, b): return a + b```), finish_reason=stop, no repetition. The VRAM split confirms the topology took effect: FFN tensors (blk.N.ffn_{down,gate,up}) landed on GPU0 (10476 MiB) and the attention+SSM+KV cache on GPU1 (7540 MiB). Coherent but ~24% SLOWER than single-GPU (30.2 vs 39.5 tok/s): a 16GB Q4 model already fits one 24GB card, so intra-model tensor split only adds cross-GPU PCIe transfer + sequential-GPU execution overhead -- no speed benefit for this model size.
configs.note_original_smoke_failure: The automated smoke run initially recorded this config as 'exited early (code 1)' due to a driver-side arg-parsing bug (the extra-args string was comma-split, which broke the `-ts 0,1` value into `-ts 0` + a stray `1`). After fixing the parser to whitespace-split, the config loads and serves coherently (validated manually 2026-07-19).

configs.error: OUT_OF_MEMORY loading the MTP draft model
configs.diagnosis: ThinkingCap-27B's GGUF DOES ship nextn MTP heads (8 tensors) + qwen35.nextn_predict_layers metadata, but in this llama.cpp build (b9606) `--spec-type draft-mtp --model-draft <same gguf>` loads a FULL SECOND 16GB copy of the model as the draft rather than reusing the in-model nextn heads in place. 2x16GB = 32GB > 24GB -> cudaMalloc failed (allocating 15339 MiB on device 0, out of memory). Qwen3.5-9B-MTP works because 2x5.5GB=11GB fits. So MTP self-draft is NOT a usable speed lever for the 27B on a 24GB card here; -otd nextn=CUDA0 cannot help because the whole 16GB draft copy (not just the nextn heads) needs a home.

configs.error: OUT_OF_MEMORY loading the MTP draft model (same root cause as single_gpu_mtp_on)
configs.diagnosis: Even split across 2 cards, MTP needs a full 16GB draft copy somewhere; GPU0 already holds ~10.5GB of offloaded FFN, so adding the 16GB draft copy OOMs. MTP self-draft infeasible for the 27B on 2x24GB in this build.

wilcoxon.note: all per-game deltas are zero (tie) -- Wilcoxon undefined

methodology_note: SEEDED induce->plan->execute on the same build_progress_window input as REQ-ARC-WMTE-5720/5724/5725; genuine-reasoning induce (no-fence /think) via the exp5724.run_reason_cell mechanism with ONLY the budget changed 8192->16384. ThinkingCap via /v1/chat/completions (chat template, the 5725 fix) on a DUAL-GPU FFN+MTP-draft split; Qwen3.5-9B via raw /completion single-GPU (its live path). Both re-measured FRESH at 16384. Servers sequential (no contention, no world_model.py race). Paired by GAME; PRIMARY metric = induce completion rate, PRIMARY test = Wilcoxon signed-rank. Real level-up count is the decisive downstream signal regardless of proxy metrics.
recommendation_scope: A CONTENT + engineering test on a 2x24GB 3090 dev rig, NOT a deployment decision. Reports (a) whether the 2x budget + larger N make ThinkingCap's completion edge over Qwen statistically distinguishable, and (b) whether the dual-GPU FFN+MTP-draft split actually speeds the 27B up vs single-GPU. NEVER flips the frozen live default (operator-only), NEVER submits, and the dual-GPU topology is a DEV-RIG approximation of Kaggle L4x4, not the submission-kernel config (a separate operator decision).
